\begin{document}
\title{Code to compute $\ell_{P}$ and detect K-unstability}

\maketitle
Let $P\subset\mathbb{R}^{n}$ be a lattice polytope which is defined
by 
\[
P=\left\{ x\in\mathbb{R}^{n}\mid\left\langle x,n_{i}\right\rangle +a_{i}\ge0,\ \forall1\le i\le d\right\} ,
\]
where $n_{i}\in\mathbb{Z}^{n}$ are primitive vectors and $a_{i}\in\mathbb{Z}$.
Let $\mathrm{d}\sigma$ be the lattice measure on the boundary $\partial P$,
which is defined as follows. Consider a facet of $P$ 
\[
F_{i}=\left\{ x\in P\mid\left\langle x,n_{i}\right\rangle +a_{i}=0\right\} .
\]
Define 
\[
\mathrm{d}\sigma|_{F_{i}}=\frac{\mathrm{d}s}{\left|n_{i}\right|}
\]
where $\mathrm{d}s$ is the Euclidean surface measure on $F_{i}$,
and $\left|n_{i}\right|$ is the Euclidean $2$-norm. Another way
to define $\mathrm{d}\sigma$: it is the Lebesgue measure on the affine
space spanned by $F_{i}$ which is normalized by the rank $n-1$ lattice
$F_{i}\cap\mathbb{Z}^{n}$. 

The relative DF invariant is 
\[
M_{\ell}(f)\coloneqq\int_{\partial P}f\mathrm{d}\sigma-\int_{P}f\ell_{P}\mathrm{d}x,\ \text{for convex }f:P\rightarrow\mathbb{R},
\]
where $\ell_{P}$ is the unique affine function such that 
\[
M_{\ell}(h)=\int_{\partial P}h\mathrm{d}\sigma-\int_{P}h\ell_{P}\mathrm{d}x=0,\ \text{for all affine function }h.
\]
Equivalently, take $h=1,x_{i}$, $\ell_{P}$ satisfies linear system:
\[
\int_{P}\ell_{P}=\left|\partial P\right|_{\mathrm{d}\sigma},\int_{P}x_{i}\ell_{P}=\int_{\partial P}x_{i}\mathrm{d}\sigma,\ i=1,\dots,n.
\]

\begin{defn}
We say $P$ is relatively K-semistable if $M_{\ell}(f)\geq0$ for
all $f\in\mathcal{C}(P)$, where $\mathcal{C}(P)$ is the space of
continuous functions on $P$. Otherwise, if $M_{\ell}(f)<0$ for some
$f\in\mathcal{C}(P)$, we say $P$ is relatively K-unstable. 
\end{defn}

\begin{fact}[Donaldson]
 when $n=2$, $P$ is relatively K-unstable if and only if there
is a simple convex function of the form 
\[
g=\max\left\{ ax+by+c,0\right\} 
\]
such that $M_{\ell}(g)<0$.
\end{fact}

Goal: 

1. compute $\ell_{P}$ precisely. 

2. develop an algorithm to test the un-stability of polygons using
the fact of Donaldson. 

3. 前面是给定多面体，探测它是否unstable. 现在我想搜索2维的relative K-unstable 格点多面体. 

输入参数：顶点个数$d$, 正整数$N$约束法向量的复杂度，$M$约束边长。

用逐步选取边向量和边长的方法来生成$P$。记 
\[
\mathcal{P}_{N}=\left\{ (a,b)\in\mathbb{Z}^{2}\mid\gcd\left(a,b\right)=1,(a,b)\neq(0,0),\left|a\right|\le N,\left|b\right|\le N\right\} 
\]
为非零primitive integer vectors构成的集合。按如下方式依次选取$d$个顶点。

取第一个顶点$v_{1}=(0,0)$, 第一个方向$p_{1}=(1,0)$。 选正整数步长$k_{1}\le M$, 得到第2个顶点$v_{2}=v_{1}+k_{1}p_{1}$。选第二个方向$p_{2}\in\mathcal{P}_{N}$使得$p_{1}$到$p_{2}$的逆时针夹角介于$0$到$\pi$之间。选正整数步长$k_{2}\le M$,
得到第3个顶点$v_{3}=v_{2}+k_{2}p_{2}$。 

一般地， 从顶点$v_{i}$ ($i\le d-1$)开始， 选前进方向$p_{i}\in\mathcal{P}_{N}$满足两个条件: 

(1) 使得$p_{i-1}$到$p_{i}$的逆时针夹角介于$0$到$\pi$之间 (可用cross product 的z分量符号检测) 

(2) $p_{i}$ 到到$-v_{i}$的逆时针夹角介于$0$到$\pi$之间; 

然后选正整数步长$k_{i}\le M$, 使得下一个顶点$v_{i+1}=v_{i}+k_{i}p_{i}$的第二分量大于0
(即$v_{i+1}$在上半平面中)。如此下去，直到得到$v_{d}$（位于上半平面）。

连接$v_{d}$和$v_{1}$, 得到一个位于上半平面的整点多边形。然后用现成的Donaldson程序探测其非稳定性. 注意边$\overline{v_{i}v_{i+1}}$的$d\sigma$测度为$k_{i}$。
边$\overline{v_{d}v_{1}}$的primitive向量和步长都没有被$M$约束。

冗余：注意$(k_{1},\dots,k_{d-1})$与$(lk_{1},\dots,lk_{d-1})$可视为等价，因为它们给出的多边形相似。搜索中记录Donaldson检测过的$(k_{1},\dots,k_{d-1})$。一旦发现新的$(k_{1},\dots,k_{d-1})$向量不是primitive的，就查看约去公因子后的向量是否已经检测过，避免重复Donaldson检测。
